Mr. Kartikey Hari Gupta, Advocate with Ms. Irum Zeba, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Pradeep Hariya, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Bhupendra Singh Bisht, Advocate for respondent no.5.
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for respondent no.6.

The petitioner in the present writ petition has put a challenge to the act of the respondents'
administration of removing and demolishing the encroachments, which has been made on Kabristan Marg in Narayan Nagar, Bara Patthar, District Nainital.
The petitioner has contended, that since he was granted license under the Food Safety Standards Act of 2006 on 16.12.2017, he had a vested right to continue the running of the tea stall under the Food Safety Standards Act of 2006.

In fact, the Food Safety Standards Act of 2006, as per its SOR, is only intended to issue a license for the purposes of permitting sale of consumable products, which specified a particular standard of quality.

Grant of a license under the said Act, in itself does not envisage or lead to an inference, that the person who is running a particular business at a place from that shop under the licence itself is has been validly constructed, on a land belonging to the petitioner and that too without any proof of title being placed on record.

The learned counsel for the petitioner had submitted, that the act of removing the encroachment by the respondents without giving any due notice, as attempted to be argued in the light of the provisions contained under Section 4 of the Uttar Pradesh Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1972, in fact if the provisions of Section 4 of the Uttar Pradesh Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1972, is taken into consideration, which is extracted hereunder:-

sentences.text: - (1) If the Prescribed Authority either of its own motion or on an application or report received on behalf of the State Government or the corporate authority, is of opinion that any, persons are in unauthorised occupation of 'any public premises' and that they should be evicted the Prescribed Authority shall issue in the manner hereinafter provided a notice in writing calling upon all persons concerned to show cause why an order of eviction should not be made.

(2) The notice shall - (a) specify the grounds on which the order of eviction is proposed to be made; and (b) require all persons concerned that is to say, all persons who are, or may be, in occupation of, or claim interest in the public premises to show cause, if any.

against the proposed order on or before such date as is specified in the notice being a date not earlier than ten days from the date of issue there of (3) The Prescribed Authority shall cause the notice to be served either personally on all those persons concerned or by having it afford on the outer door some other conspicuous part of the public premises and in any other manner.
provided in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

(4) Where the Prescribed Authority knows or has reasons to believe that many persons are in acupation of the premises, then, without prejudice to the provisions of Sub-sections (3), he shall cause a copy of the notice to be served on every such person by registered post or by delivering or tendering it to that person or in such other manner as may be prescribed."

The issuance of notice of a show cause is required to be given by the competent authority or the State agency, when there is an unauthorized occupancy of "any public premises", the pre condition under Section 4, for the issuance of notice is only required, when an eviction is to be done from a premises, which has been defined under the Act itself and not otherwise.

Under the Uttar Pradesh Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1972, in its Sub Clause (e) of Section 2 defines 'public premises,'
which is extracted hereunder:-
"(e) "public" premises means any premises belonging to or taken on lease or requisitioned by or on behalf of the State Government, and includes any premises belonging to or taken on lease by or on behalf of - (i) any company as defined in Section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956, in which not less than fifty-one per cent of the paid-up share capitals held by the State Government: or (ii) any local authority; or (iii) any Corporation (not being a company as defined in Section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956 or a local authority) owned or controlled by the State Government: or (iv) any society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, the governing body whereof consists, under the rules or regulations of the society, wholly of public WPMS/1031/2022 on 13 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52535582/
2 officers or nominees of the State Government or both:
and also includes, -
(i) Nazul land or any other premises entrusted to the management of local authority (including any building built with Government funds on land belonging to the State Government after the entrustment of the land to that local authority, not being land vested in or entrusted to the management of a Gaon Sabha or any other local authority, under any law relating to land tenures):
(ii) any premises acquired under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 with the consent of the State Government for a company (as defined in that Act) and held by that company under an agreement executed under Section 41 of that Act providing for re-entry by the State Government in certain conditions:"
In fact, in the classification of the land or a building, which will fall within the ambit of a definition of a 'public premises', would principally cannot be read in exclusion to the principal intention by the provisions contained under the definition clause of Section 2(e) of the Act, which defines to be the 'Public Premises,' which means a premises belonging to the State Government and includes the premises which are leased or requisitioned by the State, in its further sub classification it deals with the land belonging to as defined under the Companies Act, or under the Local Authority,
Corporations, Society, Nazul Land, land which is a subject matter of land acquisition and henceforth.
But in all these sub classification of land, as vested with the different bodies defined under its Sub Clauses, the pre condition is that the recourse to Section 4, would be mandatory when the aforesaid land is falling under any of the Sub Clauses of a land which has been leased or requisitioned by the State or its agencies to person who is intended to be evicted.

sentences.text: Since, that is not a situation here, where the petitioner's occupancy over the land is a land, which has been leased or requisitioned to him or it falls under any of the categories under the Sub Clauses of Sub Section (e) of Section 2, the prior issuance of notice under Section 4 of Uttar Pradesh Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, will not be applicable in the instant case, and that too this Court is of the view that equity is available to a law abiding citizen, having legal occupation under a lease or requisition.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner has also attempted to argue the writ petition, from the prospective of the implications of Article 21 of the Constitution of India, that has envisaging and guaranteed a right to livelihood.

A protection of life and liberty will not envisage a protection or granting a license to a person to continue to unauthorisedly occupy a land belonging to the State under the heads classified under Section 2(e) of the Act.

The scope of Article 21 of the Constitution of India, has to be rationally expanded to be made applicable to bring an action of the State of removing an unauthorized occupant from the land which WPMS/1031/2022 on 13 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52535582/
3 has been occupied illegally, will not entail a attraction of Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
In fact, even according to the writ petition itself, the petitioner has admitted the fact that he is in occupation of a land adjoining to the graveyard of the Muslims.

The maintenance of the graveyard and the burial places, is contained under the Schedule-7 as framed under Article 246 of the Constitution of India, and it is rather in list 2, that is the State's responsibility under Entry 10, to maintain and provide for an appropriate burial places and burial grounds, cremation and cremation grounds.

This mandate of Schedule-7, which protects the intention of Article 246 of the Constitution of India,
will in itself form to be a subject matter of a State legislature and if it is a subject matter of State legislature and there is no vesting of right to bring the land under the definition of Public Premises as defined under Section 2(e) of the Act of 1972 to which the shelter has been taken by the petitioner, the argument, as extended by the counsel is not acceptable by this Court.
Hence, the writ petition lacks merits and the same is accordingly, dismissed.

(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 13.05.2022 Arti WPMS/1031/2022 on 13 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52535582/
